deep.reconstruction:
Context. On the previous page Gauss expands the lemniscatic function P: P(xϖ) = 2.6220575x − 2.0656648x^5 − 0.5811918x^9 + 0.0245475x^13 + 0.0001890x^17 + 0.0000620x^21, with log(P/φ) = −φ^4/60 − φ^8/(8·3·25·7) − … . Here ϖ = 2.6220575… is the lemniscate constant. This P is the Weierstrass sigma function of the lemniscatic lattice (g2 = 4, g3 = 0): σ(z) = z − z^5/60 − z^9/10080 + … . For example ϖ^5/60 = 2.06566 and ϖ^9/10080 = 0.58119. Its zeros are the Gaussian-integer multiples of ϖ, and sl = P/Q.

(1) Top-left block: derivative at x = 1. With P(xϖ) = Σ c_n x^n, Gauss forms Σ n c_n:
• 2.62206 − 5·2.06566 (= 10.32832) − 9·0.58119 (= 5.23073) + 13·0.0245475 (= 0.31912) + 17·0.000189 (= 0.00321) + 21·0.000062 (= 0.00130).
• Grouped: 2.94439 − 15.55905 = −12.61466, plus 0.00130, giving ≈ −12.6134.

(2) Far-right block: second derivative. Σ n(n−1)c_n = −20·2.0656648 (41.31330) − 72·0.5811918 (41.84580) + 156·0.0245475 (3.8294) + 272·0.000189 (0.0514) = −83.15910 + 3.88080 = −79.2783. Halved, this is −39.639.

(3) Struck-out middle column. It attempts Σ n²c_n: 2.6221 + 4.4677 + 0.0546 = 7.1444 against 51.6416 + 47.0763 = 98.7177, difference 91.5733. It was abandoned.

(4) Result of the Taylor expansion: P((1+y)ϖ) = −12.614y − 39.639y² + … . In the margin Gauss puts the theoretical values 12.613 and 39.626.

(5) The functional equation that produces those values:
• P((1+y)ϖ)/e^{π(1+y)²/2} = −P(yϖ)/e^{πy²/2}, i.e. P((1+y)ϖ) = −e^{π/2} e^{πy} P(yϖ).
• Since P(yϖ) = ϖy + O(y^5), the right side is −e^{π/2}ϖ y − πe^{π/2}ϖ y² − … .
• Logarithms on the page: log ϖ = 0.4186422, log e^{π/2} = 0.6821882, sum 1.1008302 → 12.6134; adding log π = 0.4971499 → 39.627.
• This is the quasi-periodicity σ(z+ϖ) = −e^{π(z/ϖ + 1/2)} σ(z) of the lemniscatic sigma function.

(6) Corollary. Iterating gives P((1+y)ϖ)/P((−1+y)ϖ) = e^{2πy} = 1 + 2πy + … .

(7) Normalisation. Gauss considers P((a+bi)ϖ)/e^{(a²/2 + b²/2 + abi)π}. He remarks it 'scheint periodisch von a u. b zu seyn' (seems to be periodic in a and b) and renames this function P(a+bi)ϖ.
• My check: F(z+1) = −F(z).
• Using P(iu) = iP(u), F(z+i) = −e^{−2πia}F(z).
• So |F| = |σ(zϖ)|e^{−π|z|²/2} is exactly doubly periodic, and F itself is periodic up to sign/phase.

(8) Fourier (theta) expansions of the normalised function, with C = √(π/(ϖ√2)) and q = e^{−π}:
• I. P(aϖ) = C(2e^{−π/4} sin aπ − 2e^{−9π/4} sin 3aπ + 2e^{−25π/4} sin 5aπ − …) = C·θ1(πa, e^{−π}).
• II. P(a + ½i) = C(1 − 2e^{−π}cos 2aπ + 2e^{−4π}cos 4aπ − …)(sin aπ + i cos aπ) = C·θ4(πa)·i e^{−iπa}.
• The right-margin draft N(1 − 2e^{−π}cos 2aπ + …)·e^{…}(cos aπ − i sin aπ) is a preliminary form of II.

(9) My verification of the constant. Use σ(z) = (2ω/π)e^{ηz²/2ω}θ1(v)/θ1'(0) with θ1'(0) = θ3³/√2 and θ3² = √2ϖ/π at q = e^{−π}. This gives C = ϖ√2/(πθ3³) = √(π/(ϖ√2)), exactly Gauss's constant. Formula II follows from θ1(v + πτ/2) = i q^{−1/4} e^{−iv} θ4(v).

(10) Numerics, left margin:
• log 2C = 0.2650263 and log e^{π/4} = 0.3410941, with 9× and 25× multiples 3.0698468 and 8.5273522.
• log e^{π} = 1.3643764 and log e^{4π} = 5.4575054.
• C = 0.9204418, 2Ce^{−π} = 0.0795518, 2Ce^{−4π} = 0.0000064.
• I = 0.8393290 sin aπ − 0.0015674 sin 3aπ + … .
• II, real part: product-to-sum gives C(1+e^{−π}) sin aπ − C(e^{−π}+e^{−4π}) sin 3aπ + … = 0.9602177, 0.0397791, 0.0000032.
• II, imaginary part: C(1−e^{−π}) cos aπ − C(e^{−π}−e^{−4π}) cos 3aπ = 0.8806659, 0.0397727.

(11) III: P(a + ¼i).
• In general F(a+bi) = C e^{−πb²} θ1(π(a+bi)), so the coefficient of sin((2n+1)aπ) is multiplied by e^{−b²π}cosh((2n+1)bπ) and that of i cos((2n+1)aπ) by e^{−b²π}sinh((2n+1)bπ). Gauss writes this as e^{(b−bb)π} and (e^{bπ}+e^{−bπ})e^{−bbπ}/2. With b = ¼, b − b² = 3/16, hence e^{3π/16}.
• Log work: 9.9607466 − 9.9239322 = 0.0368144 = log(e^{−π/16}cosh(π/4)) = log 1.088464. Also 7.8360455 − 7.1951798 = 0.6408667 = log(e^{−π/16}cosh(3π/4)). Further 0.6408667 − 0.0368144 = 0.6040523 = log(cosh 3π/4 / cosh π/4).
• Results: III = 0.9135800 sin aπ − 0.0068556 sin 3aπ + i(0.5995204 cos aπ − 0.0067336 cos 3aπ) + … .
errors: III, imaginary part: the coefficient of cos aπ should be 2Ce^{−π/4}·e^{−π/16}sinh(π/4) = 0.839329 × 0.713808 = 0.5991202, not 0.5995204 (error 4.0e-4). This assumes the reading 0,5995204 is correct. The cos 3aπ coefficient 0.0067336 and both sin coefficients (0.9135800, 0.0068556) are correct.
The struck-out middle column uses 4.4677 for the 13th-order term (should be 169·0.0245475 = 4.1485 if Σn²c_n was intended); 98.7177 − 7.1444 = 91.5733. Gauss abandoned the column.

In the top-left sum the 21st-order term (+0.00130) is listed separately; the final derivative is ≈ −12.6134, matching e^{π/2}ϖ = 12.6134. The empirical second coefficient 39.639 vs theoretical 39.627 reflects truncation of the series.
The bracket for the modified function is written (e^{bπ}+e^{−bπ})/(2e^{−bbπ}); the factor e^{−bbπ} should multiply, not divide (the computation itself uses it correctly via e^{(b−bb)π}).
'Scheint periodisch' is only approximately right: F(z+1) = −F(z), and F(z+i) = −e^{−2πia}F(z). Only |F| is genuinely doubly periodic.

results.what: Quasi-periodicity of the lemniscatic P (sigma) function: P((1+y)ϖ) = −e^{π/2}e^{πy}P(yϖ), equivalently P((1+y)ϖ)/P((−1+y)ϖ) = e^{2πy}; verified numerically against the power series
results.modern_name: Quasi-periodicity of the Weierstrass sigma function, σ(z+2ω) = −e^{2η(z+ω)}σ(z), lemniscatic case with Legendre relation
results.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass (sigma function, 1860s–1880s); Abel/Jacobi for theta analogues; Gauss's lemniscatic P,Q known from Werke III

results.what: Normalised function P(zϖ)e^{−π(a²+b²)/2 − iπab}, observed to be (quasi-)periodic in a and b
results.modern_name: Normalised (Hermitian) theta/sigma function |σ(z)|e^{−π|z|²/2A}, a doubly periodic modulus (Kronecker/Arakelov-type normalisation)
results.usually_credited_to: Kronecker (1880s) for related non-holomorphic normalisations; standard in 20th-century theta-function theory

results.what: Theta-series expansion P(aϖ) = √(π/(ϖ√2))·Σ(−1)^n 2e^{−(2n+1)²π/4} sin((2n+1)aπ), with the exact constant
results.modern_name: σ(z) expressed through Jacobi θ1 at q = e^{−π} (lemniscatic case), θ3² = √2ϖ/π
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (Fundamenta Nova 1829) / Abel; Gauss's lemniscatic theta expansions published posthumously in Werke III

results.what: Expansions on the shifted lines a + ½i and a + ¼i: θ4 factor times (sin aπ + i cos aπ), and the cosh/sinh-weighted series with e^{−b²π}
results.modern_name: Half-period translation θ1(v+πτ/2) = i q^{−1/4}e^{−iv}θ4(v); Fourier expansion of theta functions off the real axis

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's lemniscatic P/Q functions, their quasi-periodicity and theta-type expansions are known from his Nachlass (Werke III). The page is a careful numerical verification of these. The only mildly notable feature is the explicit non-holomorphic normalisation e^{−π(a²+b²)/2} making the function look doubly periodic, which anticipates later Kronecker-style normalisations but is easily seen as a working device.
